checks: Immediate-observation migration executes and is repeatable on PostgreSQL.
Invalid device credentials cannot update hardware state.
A compact OFF observation persists the actual decoded state, with no raw timings or telemetry/history insertion.
The database trigger emits a private, controller-scoped state payload without device credentials.
Duplicate and reordered sequence uploads neither rewrite state nor emit extra broadcasts.
An older boot arriving late cannot overwrite the newer capture.
A new physical capture with the same settings refreshes the observation; only capture-identity retries are deduplicated.
Noise, auxiliary packets, raw timings, malformed power/features/sequence/temperature and oversized payloads are rejected.
Each device credential updates only its own registered controller.
A Broadcast failure preserves the observation and Postgres Changes fallback.
Legacy captures remain compatible and Broadcast strips their top-level and nested raw timing data.
Admin-only reception and server-only publishing remain enforced even alongside pre-existing broad policies; unrelated topics keep their policies.
Anonymous hardware can use its credential-scoped observation RPC without direct table access.
The immediate RPC also installs and persists successfully when Broadcast services are unavailable.
